I can't make a strong case for buying SARP, and the brief doesn't support one.

The signals point the other way. The class is OPERATOR, but the curve data shows a single cluster: bundle_share and top3_share are both 1.0, and the top five buyers took 99.9% of the first two minutes after graduation. Launch bots were present. That is coordinated accumulation, not organic demand. Operator-backed coins have been roughly break-even on average, and that average assumes the operator hasn't already positioned to exit.

The last-15-minute flow is weak for a coin that has returned 1310x in 30 minutes. Sells were 7.99 SOL against 12.4 SOL of buys, and net flow was only 4.42 SOL across 50 buyers and 28 sellers. The return over those 15 minutes was +0.28%, which means momentum has flattened at the top. Buyers are thin relative to the pool depth of 3,081 SOL, and a $20 ticket on a coin with a $63M market cap and a 1310x run is buying the exit liquidity the operator is standing on.

The name and symbol are not a reason to buy either. "Strategic American Protocol" is a generic label with no supporting data in the brief.
